question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A solution for all difficulties or diseases.
explanation: Option A is correct. A 'Panacea' is a supposed cure for all diseases or problems. Option B (Elixir) refers to a magical or medicinal potion, often believed to grant eternal life. Option C (Antidote) is a medicine taken to counteract a specific poison. Option D (Anesthetic) is a substance that induces insensitivity to pain.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An inscription on a tombstone in the memory of the person who has died.
explanation: Option B is correct. An 'Epitaph' is a phrase or form of words written in memory of a person who has died, especially as an inscription on a tombstone. Option A (Epilogue) is a section or speech at the end of a book or play. Option C (Epitome) is a person or thing that is a perfect example of a particular quality or type. Option D (Epigraph) is an inscription on a building, statue, or coin.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Something no longer in use.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Obsolete' refers to something that is no longer produced or used; out of date. Option A (Absolute) means complete or not qualified in any way. Option C (Outdated) is a close synonym but 'Obsolete' is the exact formal one-word substitution. Option D (Ancient) means belonging to the very distant past.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who can endure pain or hardship without showing his feelings or complaining.
explanation: Option B is correct. A 'Stoic' is a person who can endure pain or hardship without showing their feelings or complaining. Option A (Ascetic) is a person who practices severe self-discipline and abstains from all forms of indulgence. Option C (Cynic) is a person who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest. Option D (Skeptic) is a person inclined to question or doubt accepted opinions.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Someone who makes charitable donations intended to increase human wellbeing.
explanation: Option B is correct. An 'Altruist' (or Philanthropist) is someone who makes charitable donations intended to increase human well-being. Option A (Philatelist) is a person who collects or studies stamps. Option C (Somnambulist) is a person who walks in their sleep. Option D (Egoist) is a self-centered or selfish person.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An extreme fear of being in a small confined place.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Claustrophobia' is the extreme or irrational fear of confined places. Option A (Agoraphobia) is the fear of open or public places. Option B (Acrophobia) is the extreme fear of heights. Option D (Hydrophobia) is the extreme fear of water.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Handwriting which is difficult or impossible to read.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Illegible' means not clear enough to be read. Option B (Illiterate) refers to a person who is unable to read or write. Option C (Infallible) means incapable of making mistakes or being wrong. Option D (Incorrigible) refers to a person or their behavior that is not able to be corrected or changed.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Something that cannot be heard.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Inaudible' means unable to be heard. Option A (Inevitable) means certain to happen; unavoidable. Option C (Inaccessible) means unable to be reached. Option D (Invincible) means too powerful to be defeated or overcome.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who helps another to commit a crime or to do something morally wrong.
explanation: Option A is correct. An 'Accomplice' is a person who helps another commit a crime. Option B (Mercenary) is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army, usually motivated purely by money. Option C (Pedant) is a person who is excessively concerned with minor details and rules. Option D (Veteran) is a person who has had long experience in a particular field.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who is difficult to please.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Fastidious' refers to someone who is very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail; difficult to please. Option B (Fatalist) is someone who feels that no matter what he or she does, the outcome will be the same because it's predetermined. Option C (Fugitive) is a person who has escaped from captivity or is in hiding. Option D (Fanatic) is a person filled with excessive and single-minded zeal.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Able to use the left hand and right hand equally well.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Ambidextrous' describes a person able to use the right and left hands equally well. Option A (Ambiguous) means open to more than one interpretation; not having one obvious meaning. Option C (Ambivalent) means having mixed feelings or contradictory ideas about something. Option D (Introvert) is a shy, reticent person.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Hard but liable to break easily.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Brittle' describes something that is hard but liable to break or shatter easily (like glass). Option A (Pliable) means easily bent; flexible. Option B (Elastic) means able to resume its normal shape spontaneously after being stretched. Option D (Tenacious) means tending to keep a firm hold of something; clinging or adhering closely.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who eats human flesh.
explanation: Option B is correct. A 'Cannibal' is a person who eats the flesh of other human beings. Option A (Carnivore) is an animal that feeds on flesh. Option C (Herbivore) is an animal that feeds on plants. Option D (Omnivore) is an animal or person that eats food of both plant and animal origin.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person employed to drive a private or hired car.
explanation: Option A is correct. A 'Chauffeur' is a person employed to drive a private or rented automobile. Option B (Jockey) is a person who rides in horse races, especially as a profession. Option C (Curator) is a keeper or custodian of a museum or other collection. Option D (Invigilator) is a person whose job is to keep watch over candidates at an examination.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Belonging to the same time or a person living in the same age with another.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Contemporary' refers to living or occurring at the same time. Option B (Cosmopolitan) refers to a person who is familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures. Option C (Centenarian) is a person who is one hundred or more years old. Option D (Colleague) is a person with whom one works in a profession or business.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who leaves his country to live in another.
explanation: Option B is correct. An 'Emigrant' is a person who leaves their own country in order to settle permanently in another (Exit). Option A (Immigrant) is a person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country (Into). Option C (Vagrant) is a person without a settled home or regular work who wanders from place to place. Option D (Itinerant) is a person who travels from place to place.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: To free somebody from all blame.
explanation: Option B is correct. To 'Exonerate' means to officially absolve someone from blame. Option A (Extradite) means to hand over a person accused or convicted of a crime to the jurisdiction of the foreign state in which the crime was committed. Option C (Indict) means to formally accuse of or charge with a serious crime. Option D (Incarcerate) means to imprison or confine.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A speech or a presentation made without previous preparation.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Extempore' refers to spoken or done without preparation. Option A (Maiden) refers to being or involving the first attempt or act of its kind (e.g., maiden speech). Option C (Verbatim) means in exactly the same words as were used originally. Option D (Soliloquy) is an act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when by oneself, especially by a character in a play.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An animal that lives in groups or tending to associate with others of one's kind.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Gregarious' refers to a person or animal fond of company; sociable. Option B (Gullible) means easily persuaded to believe something. Option C (Garrulous) means excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters. Option D (Glutton) is an excessively greedy eater.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who is easily deceived.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Gullible' describes someone who is easily deceived or tricked. Option B (Credible) means able to be believed; convincing. Option C (Infallible) means incapable of making mistakes. Option D (Invincible) means too powerful to be defeated.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who cannot be corrected or one who is beyond reform.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Incorrigible' refers to a person or their tendencies not able to be corrected, improved, or reformed. Option B (Ineligible) means legally or officially unable to be considered for a position or benefit. Option C (Inevitable) means certain to happen. Option D (Indelible) means making marks that cannot be removed (like ink or a memory).

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Something that cannot be avoided.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Inevitable' means certain to happen and unable to be avoided or prevented. Option B (Infallible) means never failing or making mistakes. Option C (Inaudible) means unable to be heard. Option D (Incomprehensible) means not able to be understood.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who cannot make a mistake.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Infallible' refers to someone who is incapable of making mistakes or being wrong. Option B (Incorrigible) means a person not able to be corrected or reformed. Option C (Invincible) means too powerful to be defeated. Option D (Indefatigable) refers to a person persisting tirelessly without getting fatigued.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who writes and edits dictionaries.
explanation: Option C is correct. A 'Lexicographer' is a person who compiles dictionaries. Option A (Cartographer) is a person who draws or produces maps. Option B (Choreographer) is a person who composes the sequence of steps and moves for a performance of dance. Option D (Calligrapher) is a person who is skilled in the art of beautiful handwriting.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who dislikes women.
explanation: Option B is correct. A 'Misogynist' is a person who dislikes, despises, or is strongly prejudiced against women. Option A (Misanthrope) is a person who dislikes humankind and avoids human society. Option C (Misogamist) is a person who hates the institution of marriage. Option D (Philanthropist) is a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by the generous donation of money.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Well-known for being bad or a person of evil reputation.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Notorious' refers to being famous or well-known, typically for some bad quality or deed. Option A (Famous), Option B (Eminent), and Option D (Illustrious) all refer to being well-known, respected, and admired for past achievements or good qualities.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: To give up one's authority or throne.
explanation: Option A is correct. To 'Abdicate' means to formally renounce a throne or high office. Option B (Usurp) is the exact opposite, meaning to take a position of power illegally or by force. Option C (Inherit) means to receive money, property, or a title as an heir. Option D (Crown) means to officially place a crown on the head of a new monarch.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Animals that can live on land and in water.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Amphibians' are cold-blooded vertebrate animals (like frogs) that can live both on land and in water. Option A (Mammals) are warm-blooded animals that nourish their young with milk. Option B (Reptiles) are cold-blooded animals with scales. Option D (Avians) relates to birds.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A situation in a country or organization in which there is no government, order, or control.
explanation: Option D is correct. 'Anarchy' is a state of disorder due to the absence or non-recognition of authority or government. Option A (Monarchy) is a form of government with a monarch (king/queen) at the head. Option B (Democracy) is a system of government by the whole population. Option C (Autocracy) is a system of government by one person with absolute power.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: The study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Archaeology' is the study of human history through the excavation of sites and analysis of artifacts. Option A (Anthropology) is the study of human societies, cultures, and their development. Option C (Paleontology) is the branch of science concerned with fossil animals and plants. Option D (Geology) is the science that deals with the earth's physical structure and substance.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An account of a person's life written by self.
explanation: Option C is correct. An 'Autobiography' is an account of a person's life written by that person. Option A (Biography) is an account of someone's life written by someone else. Option B (Memoir) is a historical account or biography written from personal knowledge. Option D (Bibliography) is a list of the books referred to in a scholarly work.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A place where birds are kept.
explanation: Option A is correct. An 'Aviary' is a large enclosure for confining birds. Option B (Apiary) is a place where bees are kept. Option C (Aquarium) is a transparent tank of water in which live fish and other water creatures and plants are kept. Option D (Zoo) is an establishment which maintains a collection of wild animals.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who is a great lover of books.
explanation: Option D is correct. A 'Bibliophile' is a person who collects or has a great love of books. Option A (Philanthropist) is a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, usually through donations. Option B (Misogynist) is a person who dislikes women. Option C (Philatelist) is a person who collects or studies stamps.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Words uttered impiously about God or the act of speaking irreverently about sacred things.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Blasphemy' is the act or offense of speaking sacrilegiously about God or sacred things. Option A (Bellicose) means demonstrating a willingness to fight. Option C (Benediction) is the utterance or bestowing of a blessing. Option D (Benefactor) is a person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Chronology' is the arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence. Option A (Topography) is the arrangement of the natural and artificial physical features of an area. Option B (Cartography) is the science or practice of drawing maps. Option D (Demography) is the study of statistics such as births, deaths, income, or the incidence of disease.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A short speech at the end of a play.
explanation: Option C is correct. An 'Epilogue' is a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened. Option A (Prologue) is a separate introductory section of a literary or musical work. Option B (Monologue) is a long speech by one actor in a play or movie. Option D (Dialogue) is a conversation between two or more people.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who eats too much.
explanation: Option B is correct. A 'Glutton' is an excessively greedy eater. Option A (Gourmet) is a connoisseur of good food; a person with a discerning palate. Option C (Ascetic) is a person who practices severe self-discipline and abstains from all forms of indulgence. Option D (Epicure) is a person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Holding an office without receiving a pay.
explanation: Option D is correct. 'Honorary' refers to a title or position conferred as an honor, without the usual requirements or functions, and without payment. Option A (Mercenary) refers to a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army, motivated by money. Option B (Sinecure) is a position requiring little or no work but giving the holder status or financial benefit. Option C (Voluntary) means done, given, or acting of one's own free will.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Extreme fear of water.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Hydrophobia' is the extreme or irrational fear of water. Option A (Acrophobia) is the extreme or irrational fear of heights. Option C (Agoraphobia) is the extreme or irrational fear of crowded spaces or enclosed public places. Option D (Pyromania) is an obsessive desire to set fire to things.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who suffers from an imaginary illness.
explanation: Option C is correct. A 'Hypochondriac' is a person who is abnormally anxious about their health and believes they have an illness when they do not. Option A (Cynic) is a person who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest. Option B (Optimist) is a person who tends to be hopeful and confident about the future. Option D (Pessimist) is a person who tends to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who cannot read or write.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Illiterate' refers to a person who is unable to read or write. Option A (Illegible) refers to handwriting or text that is not clear enough to be read. Option C (Infallible) refers to someone who is incapable of making mistakes. Option D (Invincible) refers to someone who is too powerful to be defeated.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: That which cannot be satisfied.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Insatiable' refers to an appetite or desire that is impossible to satisfy. Option B (Inevitable) means certain to happen and unavoidable. Option C (Incorrigible) means a person or their tendencies that are not able to be corrected, improved, or reformed. Option D (Indelible) means making marks that cannot be removed.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who dies without a will.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Intestate' refers to a person who has died without having made a will. Option A (Insolvent) and Option B (Bankrupt) both refer to a person or organization unable to pay debts owed. Option D (Indigent) refers to a person who is poor and needy.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you visit.
explanation: Option B is correct. An 'Itinerary' is a planned route or journey. Option A (Inventory) is a complete list of items such as property, goods in stock, or the contents of a building. Option C (Directory) is a book listing individuals or organizations alphabetically or thematically with details such as names, addresses, and telephone numbers. Option D (Dictionary) is a book that lists the words of a language and gives their meaning.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Giving undue favours to one's own kith and kin.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Nepotism' is the practice among those with power or influence of favoring relatives or friends, especially by giving them jobs. Option A (Despotism) is the exercise of absolute power, especially in a cruel and oppressive way. Option C (Plagiarism) is the practice of taking someone else's work or ideas and passing them off as one's own. Option D (Chauvinism) is exaggerated or aggressive patriotism.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Government or rule by a small group of people.
explanation: Option D is correct. An 'Oligarchy' is a small group of people having control of a country, organization, or institution. Option A (Aristocracy) is the highest class in certain societies, typically comprising people of noble birth holding hereditary titles and offices. Option B (Plutocracy) is government by the wealthy. Option C (Theocracy) is a system of government in which priests rule in the name of God or a god.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: That through which light cannot pass.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Opaque' refers to something not able to be seen through; not transparent. Option A (Transparent) allows light to pass through so that objects behind can be distinctly seen. Option B (Translucent) allows light, but not detailed shapes, to pass through. Option D (Luminous) refers to something that emits or reflects light; shining.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who collects or studies stamps.
explanation: Option C is correct. A 'Philatelist' is a person who collects or studies stamps. Option A (Numismatist) is a person who collects coins or medals. Option B (Philanthropist) is a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by the generous donation of money to good causes. Option D (Misologist) is a person who hates reasoning or knowledge.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Violation of something holy or sacred.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Sacrilege' is the violation or misuse of what is regarded as sacred. Option A (Privilege) is a special right, advantage, or immunity granted or available only to a particular person or group. Option C (Sabotage) is the act of deliberately destroying, damaging, or obstructing something, especially for political or military advantage. Option D (Pilgrimage) is a pilgrim's journey, typically to a religious or sacred place.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: The period between the beginning of puberty and adulthood.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Adolescence' is the period following the onset of puberty during which a young person develops from a child into an adult. Option A (Senescence) is the condition or process of deterioration with age. Option B (Infancy) is the state or period of early childhood or babyhood. Option D (Antiquity) refers to the ancient past, especially the period before the Middle Ages.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting.
explanation: Option B is correct. An 'Agenda' is a formal list of items to be discussed at a formal meeting. Option A (Schedule) is a plan for carrying out a process or procedure, giving lists of intended events and times. Option C (Timetable) is a chart showing the departure and arrival times of transport. Option D (Register) is an official list or record.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A partial or total loss of memory.
explanation: Option A is correct. 'Amnesia' is a partial or total loss of memory. Option B (Nostalgia) is a sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past. Option C (Insomnia) is a sleep disorder characterized by an inability to sleep. Option D (Dementia) is a chronic or persistent disorder of the mental processes caused by brain disease.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An official pardon or the formal act of liberating someone.
explanation: Option C is correct. 'Amnesty' is an official pardon for people who have been convicted of political offenses. Option A (Acquittal) is a judgment that a person is not guilty of the crime with which the person has been charged. Option B (Absolution) is formal release from guilt, obligation, or punishment. Option D (Exoneration) is the action of officially absolving someone from blame.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: The date on which an event happened in some previous year.
explanation: Option B is correct. An 'Anniversary' is the date on which an event took place in a previous year. Option A (Millennium) refers to a period of a thousand years. Option C (Centennial) relates to a hundredth anniversary. Option D (Decade) refers to a period of ten years.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A glass tank where fish and water plants are kept.
explanation: Option C is correct. An 'Aquarium' is a transparent tank of water in which fish and other water creatures and plants are kept. Option A (Aviary) is a large enclosure for keeping birds. Option B (Apiary) is a place where bees are kept. Option D (Terrarium) is a vivarium for smaller land animals, especially reptiles, amphibians, or terrestrial invertebrates.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A large body of water with many islands.
explanation: Option D is correct. An 'Archipelago' is an extensive group of islands, or a sea or stretch of water containing many islands. Option B (Isthmus) is a narrow strip of land with sea on either side, forming a link between two larger areas of land. Option C (Strait) is a narrow passage of water connecting two seas.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: The place where public, government or historical records are kept.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Archives' is a collection of historical documents or records providing information about a place, institution, or group of people. Option A (Museum) is a building in which objects of historical, scientific, artistic, or cultural interest are stored and exhibited. Option C (Scullery) is a small kitchen or room at the back of a house used for washing dishes. Option D (Pantry) is a small room or closet in which food, dishes, and utensils are kept.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A government by the nobles or persons of highest social order.
explanation: Option C is correct. An 'Aristocracy' is a form of government in which power is held by the nobility or the highest social class. question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who denies oneself ordinary bodily pleasures.
explanation: Option C is correct. An 'Ascetic' is a person who practices severe self-discipline and abstains from all forms of indulgence, typically for religious reasons. question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who does not believe in God.
explanation: Option D is correct. An 'Atheist' is a person who disbelieves or lacks belief in the existence of God or gods. Option C (Heretic) is a person believing in or practicing religious heresy (unorthodox beliefs).

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: Animals that eat meat.
explanation: Option B is correct. 'Carnivorous' refers to an animal that feeds on flesh. Option A (Herbivorous) refers to an animal that feeds on plants. Option C (Omnivorous) refers to an animal or person that eats food of both plant and animal origin. Option D (Cannibal) refers to a person or animal that eats the flesh of its own species.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A person who draws or makes maps.
explanation: Option C is correct. A 'Cartographer' is a person who draws or produces maps. Option A (Lexicographer) is a person who compiles dictionaries. Option B (Choreographer) is a person who composes the sequence of steps and moves for a dance performance. Option D (Calligrapher) is a person skilled in the art of beautiful handwriting.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A complete list of books.
explanation: Option C is correct. A 'Catalogue' is a complete list of items, typically one in alphabetical or other systematic order. Option A (Bibliography) is a list of the books referred to in a scholarly work. Option B (Glossary) is an alphabetical list of terms or words found in or relating to a specific subject with explanations. Option D (Index) is an alphabetical list of records or pointers.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: One who plans the steps and moves in a dance.
explanation: Option B is correct. A 'Choreographer' is a person who composes the sequence of steps and moves for a performance of dance. Option C (Producer) is a person responsible for the financial and managerial aspects of making a movie or broadcast. Option D (Composer) is a person who writes music.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: An assembly of worshippers or a gathering at a religious place.
explanation: Option C is correct. A 'Congregation' is a group of people assembled for religious worship. Option A (Mob) is a large crowd of people, especially one that is disorderly and intent on causing trouble or violence. Option B (Crowd) is a large number of people gathered together in a disorganized or unruly way. Option D (Audience) is the assembled spectators or listeners at a public event, such as a play, movie, or concert.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A man who knows a lot about things like food, music, and art.
explanation: Option B is correct. A 'Connoisseur' is an expert judge in matters of taste, such as fine arts, food, or music. Option C (Philistine) is a person who is hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts. Option D (Amateur) is a person who engages in a pursuit on an unpaid basis.

question_text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given phrase: A man who is recovering from illness.
explanation: Option D is correct. A 'Convalescent' is a person recovering from an illness or medical treatment. Option A (Hypochondriac) is a person who is abnormally anxious about their health.
